data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA in Focus brief summarizes PISA 2015 results for collaborative problem solving, reporting cross-country mean performance and gender differences, as well as associations between collaborative problem-solving performance and students’ attitudes toward collaboration. It also reports “relative performance” defined as residuals from a pooled linear regression of collaborative problem-solving performance on performance in the core PISA subjects (science, reading and mathematics), and it presents differences after accounting for gender and students’ and schools’ socio-economic profile. The brief further links collaboration performance to school climate indicators (e.g., not being threatened, fair treatment by teachers) and to students’ reported activities outside school (e.g., internet/chat/social networks, video games, household work). Because this is a secondary reporting document, the extraction does not provide technical details on plausible-value handling, missing-data procedures, or the exact weighting/replicate design used for the reported estimates.
